topics.title: Network Performance Metrics
topics.description: Network performance metrics are parameters used to measure the efficiency, speed, reliability, and quality of a computer network. These metrics help evaluate how well a network is performing under different conditions.

subtopics.title: What are Network Performance Metrics
subtopics.theory: Network performance metrics are quantitative measures used to evaluate the efficiency and reliability of a network. These metrics help engineers understand how well data is being transmitted across the network and identify potential bottlenecks or performance issues. Network administrators use these metrics to monitor network health and optimize performance.

subtopics.title: Importance of Measuring Network Performance
subtopics.theory: Measuring network performance helps organizations ensure reliable communication, maintain quality of service, and detect network problems early. Performance monitoring is essential for maintaining high availability in applications such as cloud computing, video streaming, online gaming, and enterprise networks.

subtopics.title: What is Bandwidth
subtopics.theory: Bandwidth refers to the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted through a network connection in a given amount of time. It represents the capacity of the communication channel and is typically measured in bits per second such as Mbps or Gbps. Higher bandwidth allows more data to be transmitted simultaneously.

subtopics.title: Factors Affecting Bandwidth
subtopics.theory: Bandwidth can be affected by the physical transmission medium, network infrastructure, and hardware limitations. Technologies such as fiber optics provide significantly higher bandwidth compared to traditional copper cables.

subtopics.title: What is Throughput
subtopics.theory: Throughput refers to the actual rate at which data is successfully transmitted across a network. While bandwidth represents the maximum theoretical capacity, throughput represents the real-world performance of the network after accounting for overhead, congestion, and packet loss.

subtopics.title: Difference Between Bandwidth and Throughput
subtopics.theory: Bandwidth represents the maximum possible data transfer rate of a network while throughput represents the actual data transfer rate achieved during communication. Due to network overhead and congestion, throughput is usually lower than bandwidth.

subtopics.title: What is Latency
subtopics.theory: Latency is the time taken for a data packet to travel from the source device to the destination device across the network. It is typically measured in milliseconds. Low latency is important for real-time applications such as online gaming, video conferencing, and financial trading systems.

subtopics.title: Types of Network Delay
subtopics.theory: Network latency is influenced by several types of delay including propagation delay, transmission delay, processing delay, and queueing delay. These delays collectively determine the overall time required for packets to travel through the network.

subtopics.title: What is Packet Loss
subtopics.theory: Packet loss occurs when data packets traveling through a network fail to reach their destination. This may happen due to network congestion, faulty hardware, or transmission errors. When packets are lost, protocols such as TCP must retransmit the missing packets which increases network traffic and delay.

subtopics.title: Impact of Packet Loss
subtopics.theory: Packet loss can significantly degrade network performance. It causes interruptions in data streams, reduces throughput, and negatively affects applications such as video streaming, voice communication, and online gaming.

subtopics.title: What is Jitter
subtopics.theory: Jitter refers to the variation in packet delay during transmission across a network. Instead of arriving at consistent intervals, packets may arrive earlier or later than expected. High jitter can disrupt real-time communication applications such as VoIP and video conferencing.

subtopics.title: Managing Network Jitter
subtopics.theory: Jitter can be reduced using techniques such as buffering, traffic prioritization, and quality of service mechanisms. These techniques help maintain consistent packet delivery intervals in real-time communication systems.

subtopics.title: What is Quality of Service
subtopics.theory: Quality of Service (QoS) refers to mechanisms used in networks to prioritize certain types of traffic over others. For example voice or video traffic may be prioritized over regular data traffic to ensure smooth communication.

subtopics.title: Importance of QoS in Modern Networks
subtopics.theory: QoS is important for maintaining performance in networks that support multiple applications simultaneously. It ensures that critical services receive sufficient bandwidth and low latency even during periods of heavy network usage.
